items.title: Ambulance delays contributed to two Darwin patient deaths, coroner finds

items.title: Cutting cigarette tax will not create more smokers, Angus Taylor says

children.content: The opposition leader says slashing the tax on a pack of cigarettes by more than $20 will not lead to more smokers, as the cost of illegal cigarettes is already at that price.

articles.title: One Nation, Coalition bank on cheap cigarettes being uncool

children.content: The Coalition and One Nation will have to prove they believe a generation that has grown up thinking cigarettes are both uncool and expensive will continue to resist when the last of those barriers disappears.

items.title: First-time mum 'frightened' to feed her newborn after varying advice

children.content: First-time mother Maddy Barrett was worried she was "starving" her baby when she could not get her newborn to latch properly. She endured months of different advice from multiple practitioners, which left her feeling scared.

items.title: Negotiations over 'Australia's biggest shortcut' near an end

children.content: Years of complex land access negotiations with multiple traditional owner groups appear to be nearing an end, paving the way for the sealing of an outback highway dubbed "Australia's biggest shortcut".

items.title: The ACT's 99-year leases are expiring — what does that mean for home owners?

children.content: The ACT is the only jurisdiction in Australia that operates under a leasehold system, meaning every home owner is actually a lessee. With the first of those leases coming up for renewal, there are questions about the leasing system's origin and ongoing relevance.

image.altText: The roofs of houses with solar panels on them, as seen from above.

items.title: This is what happens when meditation goes wrong

children.content: In recent years, there has been a huge uptake in meditation, promoted to improve mental and physical health. But it can be harmful for some people.
